title: consolidate chatv1 stream framing, toolcall envelope, and stop/logprob fidelity for v1/chat.completions parity
author: Leah Ortiz
release_notes: Stabilizes v1/chat.completions streaming and improves parity for stop/logprob and toolcall structured output. No user-facing behavior changes expected unless relying on legacy stream framing.
description: Context and motivation: We continue to converge Redwood's chat API on OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics to reduce surprise for customers using the compatibility layer. This PR targets three tightly-coupled areas: (1) stream framing and heartbeat/backpressure behavior, (2) canonical handling of stop sequences and logprob emission for parity with OpenAI edge cases, and (3) a structured 'toolcall envelope' that preserves tool metadata across fragmentation and reconnection. Summary of work: Implemented a stream unifier that normalizes partial-delta framing into a stable delivery envelope (runtime/stream/coordinator.go and api/v1/stream_adapter.py), added a small heartbeat and exponential jittered backoff to improve reconnect stability, and introduced a canonical stop/logprob serializer that reconciles token-level logprobs for both aggregated and incremental modes. Also added a toolcall-envelope module (api/v1/tool_envelope.py) that packages tool metadata (name, args, result-hash, provenance) so fragments can be re-assembled deterministically on the client. Checklist: - [x] Implement stream unifier and framing rules - [x] Add heartbeat+backoff and tests for reconnect scenarios - [x] Implement stop/logprob serializer with unit tests for edge cases (empty stop, overlapping stops, repeated tokens) - [x] Toolcall envelope schema + roundtrip tests - [x] Update integration tests against the OpenAI-compat harness - [x] Docs: API compatibility notes and migration guidance (docs/api/openai_compat.md) Commits (high level): 1) stream: normalize-fragments-and-heartbeat 2) parity: stop-logprob-canonicalizer 3) toolcall: structured-envelope-and-reassembly 4) tests: integration-openai-harness-updates 5) docs: compat-notes-and-examples Changed areas (high level): - api/v1/chat_completions_adapter.py (adapter mapping for v1 parameters and role aliases) - api/v1/stream_adapter.py (framing normalization and heartbeat logic) - api/v1/tool_envelope.py (new module; envelope schema and serializer) - runtime/stream/coordinator.go (backpressure integration and fragment assembly) - runtime/kv/kv_cache.go (prefix caching tweaks for streaming resumption) - tests/integration/openai_compat/test_stream_parity.py - docs/api/openai_compat.md - examples/chat-tools/structured_toolcall_example.py Testing and CI: Ran the openai_compat integration harness locally and in CI. Initial CI run surfaced a flaky integration test (test_stream_resume_with_toolcall) that failed under heavy simulated packet loss; added a deterministic reassembly test and tuned the heartbeat interval from 2s->1s with exponential jitter. After the fix, full CI passed (unit+integration+lint). Review conversation summary: - Alicia Gomez (reviewer): requested that the tool envelope include a lightweight provenance hash to help customers correlate trimmed outputs; requested additional unit tests around partial logprob aggregation. - Author (Leah): replied with design note and added 3 unit tests covering provenance and repeated-stop scenarios. - Ravi Patel: asked for clearer mapping between role aliases (assistant/system/user) and the adapter; updated chat_completions_adapter with a normalization table and added doc examples. - Tom Baker: requested a brief perf microbenchmark for the stream unifier; added bench/stream_unifier_bench.go showing ~3% median latency impact under typical batch sizes and 12% improvement in error-rate under packet loss during streaming. Merge and rollout details: After 2 approvals, PR was squash-merged into main. The merge included a short migration note in docs/api/openai_compat.md and an opt-in feature flag (OPENAI_COMPAT_STREAM_UNIFIER) defaulting to on for hosted API but controllable in Dedicated/Private for staged rollouts. Post-merge actions: - Ship a canary build to staging with the opt-in disabled by default to collect latency and error metrics for 72 hours. - If metrics are within SLO envelope, flip the flag for hosted immediately and notify enterprise CS teams one week before flipping in Dedicated. Compatibility and guidance: This change aims to be backward-compatible for well-formed clients. Edge cases where behavior may differ: clients that parse raw stream fragments expecting a particular sequence of delta messages may need to switch to the new envelope parsing. Docs include migration snippet and a short Python example showing how to parse the envelope and reassemble toolcall results. Related items: ENG-7212 (parity), PM-308 (product acceptance), SUP-1142 (customer-reported streaming truncation incident). Notes for on-call and SRE: Watch for increased 5xxs in the stream ingress (k8s/service logs) and watch the 'stream.unifier.reassembly_errors' metric introduced in this PR. If the canary shows elevated errors, revert the flag and run the bench harness to reproduce. End-to-end impact: Improves robustness of streaming under network instability, brings stop/logprob behavior closer to OpenAI expectations (reducing customer surprises), and provides a deterministic toolcall envelope to make tool/function-calling integrations more reliable across reconnects and client library versions.
